title: How MyPozole started
body:
Jorge's family is from Mexico City, and the White Pozole recipe he grew up with had already been passed down for generations by the time he learned to make it himself in college. For years it was just a New Year's tradition, a pot he and his wife made every year for their own party. What changed things was watching his friends' reactions. Most of them were tasting pozole for the first time in their lives, and they loved it enough that they stopped calling it anything but "Jorge's Pozole." The name stuck, and eventually it became the business.

Getting there wasn't a straight line. Jorge had already lived through one business closing when the 2008 financial crisis took down the mortgage company he worked for. Years later, he built a children's transportation service for busy families, and COVID-19 shut that one down overnight too. Pozole is the one that stayed, built on a recipe that was never really his alone to begin with, and on the fact that most people in the U.S. have still never had it: pozole shows up on a tiny fraction of restaurant menus nationwide, and startlingly few people have even heard of it. Jorge's father has been a steady hand through all of it, the kind of family support that the recipe itself was already proof of.
sourceNote: Sourced from Jorge Bustamante's SDVoyager interview (https://sdvoyager.com/interview/inspiring-conversations-with-jorge-bustamante-of-mypozole/), fetched and summarized in the assistant's own words 2026-08-25, not quoted. The handoff packet also named 'el Restaurante' and 'Roaming Hunger' as sources; el Restaurante's MyPozole coverage could not be located via search, and Roaming Hunger's page returned a 403 and couldn't be fetched. If either turns up later, this can be expanded. Two low-materiality claims from the interview (pozole's ~2% restaurant-menu presence, ~27% U.S. awareness) are repeated here loosely ('a tiny fraction', 'startlingly few') rather than as precise stats, since I could not independently verify the interview's own sourcing for those two numbers.
